_transcription: PAGE MAP: the booklet is 12 rendered pages (idx 0-11 = printed folios 1-12), every one accounted for. idx 0 = bilingual cover (Series AABB4/3, SET-3, Q.P. Code 57/3/3, BIOLOGY (Theory), 2 hours, 35 marks, 12 printed pages, 13 questions). ENGLISH = the EVEN indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (folios 3, 5, 7, 9, 11): idx 2 instructions + Q1-Q2, idx 4 Q3-Q6, idx 6 Section B Q7-Q10, idx 8 Q11-Q13(a), idx 10 Q13(b). HINDI = the ODD indices 1, 3, 5, 7, 9; their tops were checked: idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 3 Hindi Q3, idx 5 Hindi Section B / Q7, idx 7 Hindi Q11, idx 9 Hindi Q13(a), so no English overflow onto an odd page and no parity inversion. idx 11 (folio 12) is blank apart from an asterisk and the footer. The paper is a scan and was read by vision only. Structure as printed: Section A Q1-6 @2, Section B Q7-12 @3, Section C Q13 case based @5 = 35. Instruction (iv) says internal choices exist but gives no count; the roster was built from the scheme's bare ORs and each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper: Q2, Q5, Q10 and Q13 (four alternatives). Q12 prints (a) and (b) with NO OR between them and the scheme marks both (1/2 + 1/2+1/2, then 1/2+1/2 + 1/2 = 3), so Q12 is one row; Q9 likewise (1/2 x 3 + 1 1/2). Q13(a) is a case study with three sub-parts, one row each, scheme split 2/2/1; its OR Q13(b) is a different case study (gene therapy) carried as ONE row, alternative to Q13ai, scheme split 1/3/1, the opener's shape. The generic lead-ins are left out of context. The scheme prints no void and no award-regardless note. FOLLOWER of 57/3/1: 9 of the 13 questions (and all four OR alternatives) are the opener's, reshuffled; each was read on this paper's page and its stem/context reused byte for byte from 2022-57-3-1 (this Q2=op Q2, Q3=op Q1, Q4=op Q3, Q5=op Q6, Q8=op Q7, Q9=op Q12, Q10=op Q11, Q11=op Q9, Q13=op Q13). The two figures (Q5a population schematic, Q5b age pyramid on idx 4; Q9 electrophoresis gel on idx 6) were compared against the opener's and 57/3/2's and are the same drawings; _figure notes were written off this paper's own pages. Four questions are new to this set and match no committed 2022 Biology paper: Q1 (roundworm and filarial worm), Q6 (roles of B and T lymphocytes), Q7 (Plasmodium life cycle in man) and Q12 (ethical argument for conservation; hotspot criteria and threat). Quotes straightened (Q6 prints curly single quotes, Q10 and Q12 and Q13(b) curly double quotes, Q9 curly single quotes), scientific names plain (Rhizobium, Anabaena, Plasmodium, Anopheles; Thermus aquaticus and E.coli printed underlined, carried as plain text). Typos kept as printed, as in the opener ('straight entered'). Q7 asks the student to trace a life cycle, not to draw, so no _drawFigure. No out-of-syllabus question.

questions.context: Enzyme Taq polymerase, is extracted from a eubacterial microorganism Thermus aquaticus from Yellowstone National Park in Montana, USA and isolated by Chien et al. (1976).
